about: The Tools step of night one. install-tools.sh (Mac) and install-tools.ps1 (PC) put these on the computer; --check / -Check prints one line per tool, 'OK name version' or 'MISSING name', then ALL TOOLS READY when every tool for that computer is there. A check command exits 0 when the tool is there. Mac checks assume Homebrew's folders and ~/.local/bin are on the PATH, the way install-tools.sh sets it. A null check means that computer doesn't need the tool.

tools.name: apple-developer-tools
tools.label: Apple's developer tools
tools.why: Apple's free kit that Git, Homebrew and most other tools on a Mac are built on.

tools.name: homebrew
tools.label: Homebrew
tools.why: The free installer that puts the rest of the tools on an Apple silicon Mac and keeps them up to date.

tools.name: git
tools.label: Git
tools.why: Keeps every version of your clone's files so nothing you build is ever lost.

tools.name: node
tools.label: Node
tools.why: Runs the Claude tools and many of the skills your clone uses.

tools.name: python
tools.label: Python 3.12
tools.why: Runs the helper scripts behind your skills, like NotebookLM and the dashboard.

tools.name: ffmpeg
tools.label: ffmpeg, the video tool
tools.why: Cuts, joins and converts the audio and video your skills make.

tools.name: gh
tools.label: GitHub's tool (gh)
tools.why: Signs you in to GitHub so the next step can back up your clone there.

tools.name: yt-dlp
tools.label: yt-dlp, the YouTube transcript tool
tools.why: Pulls the transcripts of your YouTube videos into your clone's library.

tools.name: obsidian
tools.label: Obsidian
tools.why: The free notes app where you read and edit everything your clone knows.
